CohortHonestDiD

R package for cohort-anchored HonestDiD sensitivity analysis in difference-in-differences designs with staggered adoption. It places the smoothness (SD) and relative-magnitude (RM) restrictions of Rambachan and Roth (2023) on each adoption cohort’s block bias, the cohort’s untreated trend relative to its comparison group at adoption, rather than on the aggregated event study. It works with the imputation and Callaway-Sant’Anna estimators. Confidence sets for average, dynamic, and cohort-specific effects come from the Conditional and C-LF procedures or, under SD, the fixed-length confidence interval (FLCI); inference on the aggregated event study is available as a benchmark.

Installation:

# install.packages("remotes")
remotes::install_github("lzy318/CohortHonestDiD")
library(CohortHonestDiD)

On Debian or Ubuntu, install the GLPK library (libglpk-dev) first; the Rglpk dependency needs it.

Source Code: GitHub

User Manual: Website with the Getting started and Detailed guide tutorials and the help pages. To read the tutorials in R, install with remotes::install_github("lzy318/CohortHonestDiD", dependencies = TRUE, build_vignettes = TRUE) and run browseVignettes("CohortHonestDiD").

Main References:

Liu, Ziyi (2026). Cohort-Anchored HonestDiD. arXiv:2509.01829.

Rambachan, Ashesh, and Jonathan Roth (2023). A More Credible Approach to Parallel Trends. Review of Economic Studies 90 (5): 2555-2591.

The inference routines adapt code from the HonestDiD package by Ashesh Rambachan and Jonathan Roth.

Report bugs: Open a GitHub issue or email zyliu2023 [at] berkeley.edu, and include a minimal reproducible example: a short script, a small data set that shows the problem, and the output of sessionInfo().
